newsitem.title: FRANCE: SOCCER-GINOLA SEEKS WAY OUT OF NEWCASTLE IMPASSE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-GINOLA SEEKS WAY OUT OF NEWCASTLE IMPASSE.

text.p: David Ginola, still dreaming of a place in France's 1998 World Cup squad, is looking for regular first team soccer elsewhere after being consigned to the Newcastle bench, the weekly magazine France Football said on Tuesday.

The skilled winger, a regular in former boss Kevin Keegan's exciting Newcastle attack but out of favour with new manager Kenny Dalglish, has asked his advisor Olivier Godallier to authorise an agent to broker a deal with Italy's Internazionale Milan.
But the magazine said Godallier now regretted the decision as the agent, Serge Scalet, is not recognised by world body FIFA.
Either way, Ginola's signed authorisation note suggests the Frenchman feels he must revive his flagging career in Italy, Spain or, as appears more likely, back in his home country.

Paris St Germain, whom Ginola left for Newcastle 18 months ago, are planning their rebuilding for next season and could afford a transfer fee which France Football puts at 20-25 million francs ($4-$5 million).

Marseille have also expressed an interest in Ginola, who grew up close to the Mediterranean port city, and they have a gap to fill on the left of their attack following the recent departure to Parma of France international Reynald Pedros.
But the former European champions may not have the means to make a bid.
Coach Gerard Gili said: "I have no idea what his sojourn in England has done for him. How good is his game today, what's his motivation?"

And Marseille's sporting director Marcel Dib said: "I think there are more chances of seeing him back at Paris St Germain. From what I know, between his salary and the transfer fee, he seems too expensive for us."
Ginola, 30, almost moved to Barcelona in the off-season, but the Catalan club's interest has since cooled.
